title: Annotatio IV §.XI: Bede — sacrament in FIGURE of bread and wine; figure at the Supper
pass_a_gloss: To Isidore of Seville there joins himself most nearly the VENERABLE BEDE, most celebrated Doctor of the British Isles, although his Name first became famous only in the eighth age — having confessed not only the Eucharistic truth openly in these words in the Commentary on Psalm 22: In place of the flesh and blood of the lamb, Christ substituted the Sacrament of His flesh and blood, in the FIGURE of bread and wine. Likewise, Commentary on Psalm 3: He gave at the Supper to the disciples the FIGURE of His sacrosanct body and blood;
pass_b_english: Next to Isidore: the VENERABLE BEDE (British Isles’ doctor; name famous mainly in the eighth age).

On Ps. 22: in place of the lamb’s flesh and blood Christ put the Sacrament of His flesh and blood in the FIGURE of bread and wine. On Ps. 3: at the Supper He gave the disciples the FIGURE of His sacrosanct body and blood.
source_text: Isidoro Hispalensi sese proximè adjungit VENERABILIS BEDA, Britannicarum Insularum Doctor celeberrimus, quanquam octavo demum seculô Nomen ejus inclaruerit, non Eucharisticam duntaxat veritatem, Comment. in 22. Ps. palam hisce confessus: Loco carnis & sanguinis agni, substituit Christus Sacramentum carnis suæ & sanguinis, in FIGURA panis & vini. Item, Comm. in Psal. 3. Dedit in Cœna discipulis FIGURAM sacrosancti corporis & sanguinis sui;
